# Inner and outer loops in "Meta-Learning for Cold-Start Personalization in Prompt-Tuned LLMs"

The paper uses MAML with two nested loops. Section 3.2 states them as follows (p. 2).

## Inner loop: task-specific prompt update (uses the **support** set)

$$\theta_i' = \theta - \alpha \nabla_{\theta} \mathcal{L}_{T_i}\big(f_{\theta};\, D_i^{support}\big)$$

- θ is the shared soft-prompt initialization. It has prompt length × LLM embedding dimension (p. 2, §3.1).
- α is the inner-loop learning rate (p. 2, §3.2).
- f_θ is the LLM conditioned on prompt θ (p. 2, §3.2).
- The LLM stays frozen. Gradients are computed only with respect to the soft prompt P, which is prepended to the input as [P; X] (p. 2, §3.3).
- At test time, the K ∈ {1, 3, 5} support interactions are "used solely for prompt adaptation" (p. 2, §4.1).

## Outer loop: meta-objective across tasks (uses the **query** set)

$$\min_{\theta} \sum_i \mathcal{L}_{T_i}\big(f_{\theta_i'};\, D_i^{query}\big)$$

- The goal is to optimize θ across many sampled user tasks so that performance after adaptation on $D_{query}$ is maximized (p. 1, Introduction).
- The adapted user is then evaluated on "a different set of queries of unseen interactions of the same user" (p. 2, §4.1).

## Data splits

Each user is treated as a task $T_i \sim p(T)$ (p. 1). Each task has a support set $D_i^{support}$ and a query set $D_i^{query}$ (p. 2, §3.1). Tasks are sampled episodically, with 1–5 interactions in the support set and 1–5 in the query set (p. 2, §3.4).

## Caveats on the equations

These equations were read from the page image by a model, so check them against the PDF before quoting.

- **Query superscript:** The converted outer-loop formula shows a garbled superscript, "$D_i^{\varphi^{uery}}$". I have written it as $D_i^{query}$ (p. 2).
- **Adapted prompt symbol:** The converted text writes the adapted prompt in the outer loop as $\theta_i$, not $\theta_i'$ (p. 2). The Introduction version uses $\theta_i$ in the same way (p. 1). Since the inner loop produces $\theta_i'$, the outer loop should be evaluating that adapted prompt, so I wrote $\theta_i'$.
- **Missing details:** The document gives the outer loop only as a minimization objective. It does not give an explicit outer-loop update rule or a meta learning rate.
